title: At the Mouth of the Strait
description: A source-grounded historical adventure about why Raffles wanted Singapore, why Johor's succession mattered, and what each side risked in February 1819.
learningObjectives: Explain why the East India Company wanted a port at the southern end of the Straits of Malacca.
Describe the disputed Johor succession and why Raffles recognised Tengku Hussein.
Evaluate the risks each stakeholder took in signing the 1819 agreements.

player.name: junior-interpreter
player.role: Junior interpreter attached to Raffles' expedition
player.brief: You carry messages, listen closely, and report what each side means. Your advice may change how fast the expedition moves and how carefully it deals with Johor's disputed throne.

sharedContext.text: In January 1819, Raffles came to Singapore looking for a British station at the southern end of the Straits. The Temenggong could help locally, but only a Sultan could lawfully grant land, and Johor's throne was disputed. You serve as a junior interpreter as these talks unfold.

endings.title: A Treaty and a New Port
endings.summary: The treaty is signed. The British gain their trading post, Hussein gains recognition, and the Temenggong gains a place in the new order. The risks do not vanish, but the settlement begins.

historicalOutcome.text: This ending matches the broad record. A treaty was signed on 6 February 1819. The Dutch protested, but the British stayed. In 1824 the dispute was settled, and Singapore grew quickly as a free port.

spans.quote: On 6 February 1819 a treaty was signed between the East India Company, represented by Raffles, Sultan Hussein and Temenggong Abdul Rahman.
The Dutch protested at once.
The dispute was finally settled by the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824, in which the Dutch withdrew their objection to the British presence in Singapore.
Raffles had declared Singapore a free port, where ships could trade without paying duties, and traders from the region moved their business there.

endings.divergence: This closely matches the historical record.
